-- =============================================================
-- 13_fingrid_warehouse.sql
-- Raw Fingrid Open Data, one row per dataset and time slot, exactly as
-- the API publishes it (no resampling, no gap filling, no clamping).
--
--   fingrid_dataset      what each dataset is (filled by src/fingrid_catalog.py)
--   fingrid_observation  the values; loaded by src/sync_fingrid.py
--   forecast_vs_actual   Fingrid's own forecasts joined to what happened
--
-- Idempotent: safe to run on every setup.
-- =============================================================

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fingrid_dataset (
    dataset_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    key         VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name        TEXT        NOT NULL,
    unit        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    kind        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
                CHECK (kind IN ('actual', 'forecast', 'capacity', 'balancing', 'emission', 'system')),
    resolution  INTERVAL    NOT NULL
);

-- Partitioned by month on start_time. Every query here filters one dataset and a
-- time range, so PostgreSQL reads only the months it needs (partition pruning) and,
-- inside each, the primary-key index (dataset_id, start_time).
-- benchmarks/index_benchmark.md measures the effect (scripts/benchmark_warehouse.py).
--
-- A database created before partitioning has a plain table: it is converted in
-- place (rows copied into monthly partitions). Views on the table are dropped first
-- and recreated below and in 14_co2_forecast.sql.
DO $$
BEGIN
    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_class WHERE relname = 'fingrid_observation' AND relkind = 'r') THEN
        DROP VIEW IF EXISTS forecast_vs_actual;
        DROP VIEW IF EXISTS co2_hourly;
        ALTER TABLE fingrid_observation RENAME TO fingrid_observation_unpartitioned;
        ALTER TABLE fingrid_observation_unpartitioned RENAME CONSTRAINT fingrid_observation_pkey TO fingrid_observation_unpartitioned_pkey;
    END IF;
END $$;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fingrid_observation (
    dataset_id  INTEGER          NOT NULL REFERENCES fingrid_dataset (dataset_id),
    start_time  TIMESTAMPTZ      NOT NULL,
    end_time    TIMESTAMPTZ      NOT NULL,
    value       DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    fetched_at  TIMESTAMPTZ      NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (dataset_id, start_time),
    CONSTRAINT ck_fingrid_observation_slot CHECK (end_time > start_time)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (start_time);

-- Safety net for a row outside every monthly partition. It stays empty, because
-- the sync and the snapshot restore create the months they write first.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fingrid_observation_default PARTITION OF fingrid_observation DEFAULT;

-- Create the monthly partitions (UTC months) covering [first_day, last_day]; existing
-- ones are left alone. Returns how many were created.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION ensure_fingrid_partitions(first_day date, last_day date)
RETURNS int LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    m       date;
    created int := 0;
BEGIN
    FOR m IN SELECT generate_series(date_trunc('month', first_day), date_trunc('month', last_day),
                                    interval '1 month')::date
    LOOP
        IF to_regclass(format('fingrid_observation_%s', to_char(m, 'YYYY_MM'))) IS NULL THEN
            EXECUTE format('CREATE TABLE %I PARTITION OF fingrid_observation FOR VALUES FROM (%L) TO (%L)',
                           format('fingrid_observation_%s', to_char(m, 'YYYY_MM')),
                           (m::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'),
                           ((m + interval '1 month')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'));
            created := created + 1;
        END IF;
    END LOOP;
    RETURN created;
END $$;

SELECT ensure_fingrid_partitions((now() - interval '450 days')::date, (now() + interval '60 days')::date);

DO $$
DECLARE lo date; hi date;
BEGIN
    IF to_regclass('fingrid_observation_unpartitioned') IS NOT NULL THEN
        SELECT min(start_time)::date, max(start_time)::date INTO lo, hi FROM fingrid_observation_unpartitioned;
        IF lo IS NOT NULL THEN
            PERFORM ensure_fingrid_partitions(lo, hi);
        END IF;
        INSERT INTO fingrid_observation SELECT * FROM fingrid_observation_unpartitioned;
        DROP TABLE fingrid_observation_unpartitioned;
    END IF;
END $$;

-- One row per 15-minute slot where both the actual value and a Fingrid forecast exist.
--   day_ahead: published once, the previous day at 12:00 Finnish time (datasets 246, 165)
--   intraday:  updated every 15 minutes; the stored value is the last update before
--              the slot (datasets 245, 166)
-- capacity_mw is the wind capacity Fingrid itself used for the forecast (dataset 268,
-- hourly), so wind errors can be expressed as a share of the fleet.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW forecast_vs_actual AS
WITH pairs (variable, product, actual_id, forecast_id) AS (
    VALUES ('wind',        'day_ahead', 75,  246),
           ('wind',        'intraday',  75,  245),
           ('consumption', 'day_ahead', 124, 165),
           ('consumption', 'intraday',  124, 166)
)
SELECT p.variable,
       p.product,
       a.start_time,
       a.value           AS actual_mw,
       f.value           AS forecast_mw,
       a.value - f.value AS error_mw,          -- positive: more than forecast
       c.value           AS capacity_mw        -- wind only, else NULL
FROM pairs p
JOIN fingrid_observation a
  ON a.dataset_id = p.actual_id
JOIN fingrid_observation f
  ON f.dataset_id = p.forecast_id
 AND f.start_time = a.start_time
LEFT JOIN fingrid_observation c
  ON p.variable = 'wind'
 AND c.dataset_id = 268
 AND c.start_time = date_trunc('hour', a.start_time);

-- 14_co2_forecast.sql
-- Forecast of the CO2 intensity of electricity consumed in Finland,
-- per hour of a Finnish calendar day. Fingrid publishes the intensity
-- only as it happens (dataset 396); this predicts it a day ahead.
--
-- Input: Fingrid's own day-ahead forecasts (published at 12:00 Finnish
-- time for the next day), combined into the residual load:
--     residual load = consumption (165) - wind (246) - solar (247)
-- Demand that wind and solar do not cover is met by imports and
-- thermal plants, so the intensity rises with it (r = 0.84 over the
-- last year).
--
-- Model, refitted for every target day D using only what was known
-- when D's forecast was made:
--   1. least-squares line  co2 = a + b * residual_load  over the 60
--      days that end two days before D (regr_intercept, regr_slope)
--   2. level correction: the line's mean error on day D-2, which
--      captures slow changes the residual load does not see (a nuclear
--      outage, import conditions)
--   3. floor: never below the lowest intensity seen in the training
--      window. On very windy days the line otherwise extrapolates below
--      anything ever measured (7% of hours; their error drops from
--      9.8 to 3.4 g). co2_unclamped keeps the line's own value, which
--      still orders the hours when several sit on the floor.
-- co2_naive is the baseline to beat: the same hour two days earlier.
--
-- Used by sql/analysis/18 (tomorrow) and 19 (backtest), so the live
-- forecast and its track record run the exact same SQL.
-- Techniques: views with FILTER aggregates, a set-returning SQL
--             function, regr_slope / regr_intercept, generate_series
-- =============================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW co2_hourly AS
SELECT
    date_trunc('hour', start_time)                                         AS hour_start,
    (date_trunc('hour', start_time) AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::date  AS day_fi,
    CASE WHEN COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 396) = 4                 -- a complete hour only
         THEN AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 396) END              AS co2_actual,
    AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 165)
      - AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 246)
      - COALESCE(AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 247), 0)            AS residual_load_mw
FROM fingrid_observation
WHERE dataset_id IN (396, 165, 246, 247)
GROUP BY date_trunc('hour', start_time);


-- Dropped first: CREATE OR REPLACE cannot change the columns a function returns.
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS co2_forecast(date, date, int);
CREATE FUNCTION co2_forecast(first_day date, last_day date, training_days int DEFAULT 60)
RETURNS TABLE (
    day_fi            date,
    hour_start        timestamptz,
    hour_fi           int,
    residual_load_mw  double precision,
    co2_forecast      double precision,
    co2_unclamped     double precision,
    co2_naive         double precision,
    co2_actual        double precision
)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    WITH days AS (
        SELECT generate_series(first_day, last_day - 1, interval '1 day')::date AS d
    ),
    fit AS (
        SELECT days.d,
               regr_intercept(x.co2_actual, x.residual_load_mw) AS a,
               regr_slope(x.co2_actual, x.residual_load_mw)     AS b,
               MIN(x.co2_actual)                                AS floor_g
        FROM days
        JOIN co2_hourly x
          ON x.day_fi >= days.d - (training_days + 1)
         AND x.day_fi <  days.d - 1
        WHERE x.co2_actual IS NOT NULL AND x.residual_load_mw IS NOT NULL
        GROUP BY days.d
    ),
    level AS (
        SELECT f.d, AVG(x.co2_actual - (f.a + f.b * x.residual_load_mw)) AS correction
        FROM fit f
        JOIN co2_hourly x ON x.day_fi = f.d - 2
        WHERE x.co2_actual IS NOT NULL AND x.residual_load_mw IS NOT NULL
        GROUP BY f.d
    )
    SELECT f.d,
           t.hour_start,
           EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.hour_start AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::int,
           t.residual_load_mw,
           GREATEST(f.a + f.b * t.residual_load_mw + COALESCE(l.correction, 0), f.floor_g),
           f.a + f.b * t.residual_load_mw + COALESCE(l.correction, 0),
           p.co2_actual,
           t.co2_actual
    FROM fit f
    JOIN co2_hourly t ON t.day_fi = f.d AND t.residual_load_mw IS NOT NULL
    LEFT JOIN level l ON l.d = f.d
    LEFT JOIN co2_hourly p ON p.hour_start = t.hour_start - interval '48 hours'
    WHERE f.b IS NOT NULL
$$;

-- =============================================================
-- 15_grid_events.sql
-- A log of unusual moments on the Finnish grid, from raw Fingrid data.
--
-- Four kinds of event, each with a threshold that is an operating
-- definition or stated relative to the data, not tuned by eye:
--   frequency_low / frequency_high
--       a 1-minute frequency sample (177) outside the Nordic normal
--       band 49.9-50.1 Hz; samples below 45 Hz are invalid (Fingrid
--       writes gaps as 0) and are skipped
--   nuclear_drop
--       Finnish nuclear output (188, 3-minute) at least 400 MW below
--       its highest value of the previous 15 minutes: a unit tripping
--       or being cut back fast
--   low_inertia
--       kinetic energy of the Nordic system (260) in the lowest 1% of
--       the requested window: little spinning mass to slow a frequency
--       fall, the situation fast reserves exist for
--   price_spike
--       imbalance price (319) of 1,000 EUR/MWh or more
--
-- Flagged samples of one kind are merged into a single event when the
-- gap between them is short (3 min for frequency, 30 min for nuclear,
-- none for the 15-minute series): the gaps-and-islands pattern.
--
-- For nuclear drops, freq_min_nearby is the lowest valid frequency
-- within 15 minutes of the event. It is a cross-check between two
-- independent sensors, and over the last year it shows that Finnish
-- nuclear drops rarely move the (Nordic-wide) frequency far: either
-- they were controlled ramps, or the brief nadir fell between the
-- 1-minute samples.
--
-- Techniques: set-returning SQL function, window frames with RANGE
--             intervals, gaps and islands (LAG + running SUM),
--             PERCENTILE_CONT, LATERAL subquery
-- =============================================================

DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS grid_events(timestamptz, timestamptz);
CREATE FUNCTION grid_events(from_ts timestamptz, to_ts timestamptz)
RETURNS TABLE (
    kind             text,
    start_time       timestamptz,
    end_time         timestamptz,
    peak             double precision,
    threshold        double precision,
    unit             text,
    samples          int,
    freq_min_nearby  double precision
)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    WITH
    freq AS (
        SELECT start_time, end_time, value
        FROM fingrid_observation
        WHERE dataset_id = 177 AND value >= 45
          AND start_time >= from_ts AND start_time < to_ts
    ),
    nuclear AS (
        SELECT start_time, end_time,
               value - MAX(value) OVER (ORDER BY start_time
                                        RANGE BETWEEN interval '15 minutes' PRECEDING
                                                  AND interval '1 second' PRECEDING) AS drop_mw
        FROM fingrid_observation
        WHERE dataset_id = 188
          AND start_time >= from_ts - interval '15 minutes' AND start_time < to_ts
    ),
    inertia AS (
        SELECT start_time, end_time, value
        FROM fingrid_observation
        WHERE dataset_id = 260 AND start_time >= from_ts AND start_time < to_ts
    ),
    inertia_limit AS (
        SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.01) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY value) AS lim FROM inertia
    ),
    flagged AS (
        SELECT CASE WHEN value < 49.9 THEN 'frequency_low' ELSE 'frequency_high' END AS kind,
               start_time, end_time, value,
               CASE WHEN value < 49.9 THEN 49.9 ELSE 50.1 END AS threshold
        FROM freq WHERE value < 49.9 OR value > 50.1
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'nuclear_drop', start_time, end_time, drop_mw, -400
        FROM nuclear WHERE drop_mw <= -400 AND start_time >= from_ts
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'low_inertia', i.start_time, i.end_time, i.value, l.lim
        FROM inertia i CROSS JOIN inertia_limit l WHERE i.value < l.lim
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'price_spike', start_time, end_time, value, 1000
        FROM fingrid_observation
        WHERE dataset_id = 319 AND value >= 1000
          AND start_time >= from_ts AND start_time < to_ts
    ),
    starts AS (
        SELECT flagged.*,
               CASE WHEN start_time - LAG(end_time) OVER (PARTITION BY kind ORDER BY start_time)
                         <= CASE kind WHEN 'nuclear_drop' THEN interval '30 minutes'
                                      WHEN 'frequency_low' THEN interval '3 minutes'
                                      WHEN 'frequency_high' THEN interval '3 minutes'
                                      ELSE interval '0' END
                    THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_new
        FROM flagged
    ),
    islands AS (
        SELECT starts.*, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY kind ORDER BY start_time) AS event_no
        FROM starts
    ),
    events AS (
        SELECT kind,
               MIN(start_time) AS start_time,
               MAX(end_time)   AS end_time,
               CASE WHEN kind IN ('frequency_high', 'price_spike') THEN MAX(value) ELSE MIN(value) END AS peak,
               MIN(threshold)  AS threshold,
               COUNT(*)::int   AS samples
        FROM islands
        GROUP BY kind, event_no
    )
    SELECT e.kind, e.start_time, e.end_time, e.peak, e.threshold,
           CASE e.kind WHEN 'nuclear_drop' THEN 'MW' WHEN 'low_inertia' THEN 'GWs'
                       WHEN 'price_spike' THEN 'EUR/MWh' ELSE 'Hz' END,
           e.samples,
           f.freq_min
    FROM events e
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT MIN(x.value) AS freq_min
        FROM fingrid_observation x
        WHERE e.kind = 'nuclear_drop'
          AND x.dataset_id = 177 AND x.value >= 45
          AND x.start_time BETWEEN e.start_time - interval '15 minutes' AND e.end_time + interval '15 minutes'
    ) f ON true
$$;

-- =============================================================
-- 13_forecast_scorecard.sql
-- How far were Fingrid's own forecasts from what actually happened?
--
-- One row per variable (wind, consumption) and forecast product:
--   day_ahead  published the previous day at 12:00 Finnish time
--   intraday   updated every 15 minutes (last update before the slot)
--
--   mae_mw               mean absolute error per 15-minute slot
--   bias_mw              mean error; positive = reality above forecast
--   rmse_mw              punishes large misses more than MAE
--   p95_abs_error_mw     95 in 100 slots missed by less than this
--   wape_pct             total absolute error / total actual, in percent
--   mae_pct_of_capacity  wind only: MAE as a share of the wind fleet
--                        that Fingrid assumed (dataset 268)
--
-- Parameters: start, end (timestamptz, end exclusive)
-- Techniques: views, ordered-set aggregates (PERCENTILE_CONT), NULLIF
-- =============================================================

SELECT
    variable,
    product,
    COUNT(*)                                                     AS slots,
    AVG(ABS(error_mw))                                           AS mae_mw,
    AVG(error_mw)                                                AS bias_mw,
    SQRT(AVG(error_mw * error_mw))                               AS rmse_mw,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ABS(error_mw))  AS p95_abs_error_mw,
    100 * SUM(ABS(error_mw)) / NULLIF(SUM(actual_mw), 0)         AS wape_pct,
    100 * AVG(ABS(error_mw)) / NULLIF(AVG(capacity_mw), 0)       AS mae_pct_of_capacity,
    AVG(actual_mw)                                               AS mean_actual_mw,
    AVG(capacity_mw)                                             AS mean_capacity_mw
FROM forecast_vs_actual
WHERE start_time >= %(start)s
  AND start_time <  %(end)s
GROUP BY variable, product
ORDER BY variable, product;

-- =============================================================
-- 17_forecast_error_vs_balancing.sql
-- What happens on the grid when the day-ahead forecasts are wrong?
--
-- net_surprise_mw = wind error - consumption error (day-ahead):
--   negative: less wind and/or more demand than forecast (system short)
--   positive: more wind and/or less demand than forecast (system long)
-- Slots are grouped in 500 MW bins (open-ended below -1500 and from
-- +1500 up). Each bin shows averages of:
--   mfrr_need   Fingrid's estimate of the mFRR energy needed (377)
--   mfrr_up     activated upward mFRR, published as values >= 0 (375)
--   mfrr_down   activated downward mFRR, published as values <= 0 (376)
-- and the median imbalance price (319). Net activation is up + down.
--
-- This is an association, not a cause: market parties trade after the
-- day-ahead forecast, and many other things move the balance.
--
-- Parameters: start, end (timestamptz, end exclusive)
-- Techniques: self-join of a view, LEFT JOINs, FLOOR binning with
--             LEAST/GREATEST, PERCENTILE_CONT, corr() aggregate
-- =============================================================

WITH surprise AS (
    SELECT w.start_time,
           w.error_mw - c.error_mw AS net_surprise_mw
    FROM forecast_vs_actual w
    JOIN forecast_vs_actual c
      ON c.start_time = w.start_time
     AND c.variable = 'consumption'
     AND c.product  = 'day_ahead'
    WHERE w.variable = 'wind'
      AND w.product  = 'day_ahead'
      AND w.start_time >= %(start)s
      AND w.start_time <  %(end)s
),
joined AS (
    SELECT s.start_time,
           s.net_surprise_mw,
           nd.value  AS mfrr_need_mw,
           up.value  AS mfrr_up_mw,
           dn.value  AS mfrr_down_mw,
           px.value  AS imbalance_price
    FROM surprise s
    LEFT JOIN fingrid_observation nd ON nd.dataset_id = 377 AND nd.start_time = s.start_time
    LEFT JOIN fingrid_observation up ON up.dataset_id = 375 AND up.start_time = s.start_time
    LEFT JOIN fingrid_observation dn ON dn.dataset_id = 376 AND dn.start_time = s.start_time
    LEFT JOIN fingrid_observation px ON px.dataset_id = 319 AND px.start_time = s.start_time
),
binned AS (
    SELECT joined.*,
           LEAST(GREATEST(FLOOR(net_surprise_mw / 500) * 500, -2000), 1500) AS bin
    FROM joined
)
SELECT
    CASE WHEN bin = -2000 THEN NULL ELSE bin END        AS bin_from_mw,
    CASE WHEN bin =  1500 THEN NULL ELSE bin + 500 END  AS bin_to_mw,
    COUNT(*)                                            AS slots,
    AVG(net_surprise_mw)                                AS mean_net_surprise_mw,
    AVG(mfrr_need_mw)                                   AS mean_mfrr_need_mw,
    AVG(mfrr_up_mw)                                     AS mean_mfrr_up_mw,
    AVG(mfrr_down_mw)                                   AS mean_mfrr_down_mw,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY imbalance_price) AS median_imbalance_price,
    AVG(imbalance_price)                                AS mean_imbalance_price,
    (SELECT corr(net_surprise_mw, mfrr_need_mw) FROM joined)              AS r_surprise_vs_mfrr_need,
    (SELECT corr(net_surprise_mw, mfrr_up_mw + mfrr_down_mw) FROM joined) AS r_surprise_vs_net_mfrr,
    (SELECT corr(net_surprise_mw, imbalance_price) FROM joined)           AS r_surprise_vs_price
FROM binned
GROUP BY bin
ORDER BY bin;
